title: Trump Guts CDC, Fires Dozens of Public Health Officials
description_short: Trump Guts CDC, Fires Dozens of Public Health Officials
description_medium: In late February 2025, the Trump administration fired or placed on administrative leave dozens of senior CDC officials, including leaders of its infectious disease and emergency response divisions. Entire research programs were defunded. The pandemic preparedness infrastructure rebuilt after COVID-19 was systematically dismantled. Public health officials warned the US was left significantly less prepared for emerging infectious disease threats. The gutting of CDC came alongside cuts to NIH research funding and elimination of the White House pandemic preparedness office established under Biden.
description_long: In February 2025, layoffs at the CDC reduced staffing for infectious-disease preparedness while the country faced bird flu, measles and other threats. NPR reported that about 750 employees were dismissed in the first wave, primarily newer and temporary workers. Current staff described losses among scientists assisting local health departments, outbreak modelers and workers screening travelers for dangerous pathogens. The Laboratory Leadership Service fellowship lost researchers who helped develop tests during fast-moving outbreaks. One dismissed fellow had been planning a Florida response to Oropouche; a communications pause had already prevented the plan from being shared with the state. Two workers deployed to a tuberculosis outbreak in Kansas City also received termination notices. A staff member said three of the CDC's 20 port health stations had no agency staff and half lacked an officer in charge. CDC advisers warned that the cuts threatened preparedness. The agency listed seven active emergency responses but did not answer NPR's questions about the full extent or operational impact of the layoffs.

title: Chris Wright Energy Secretary Accelerates Fossil Fuels and Kills Clean Energy Programs
notes: Linked DOE order read in full. It supports the specific priorities and reviews described here, but does not establish preserved claims of particular clean-energy terminations, lobbyist authorship or irreversible warming. Those claims remain a coordinator context hold.
description_short: Chris Wright Energy Secretary Accelerates Fossil Fuels and Kills Clean Energy Programs
description_medium: Energy Secretary Chris Wright — a former fracking company CEO who had publicly denied climate change — aggressively accelerated fossil fuel production permits and approvals while terminating, reversing, or defunding clean energy programs funded by the Inflation Reduction Act. Wright used the Department of Energy to serve the interests of the oil and gas industry he had led, implementing policies that industry lobbyists had written. Climate scientists warned the energy policy reversal locked in catastrophic warming scenarios that would be impossible to reverse.
description_long: Energy Secretary Chris Wright's February 5, 2025, order directed the Department of Energy to implement Trump's energy agenda. It prioritized increased production and criticized policies aimed at net-zero emissions as costly and harmful to reliability. The department would review its research portfolio and emphasize fossil fuels, advanced nuclear, geothermal and hydropower, alongside fusion, computing and other technology. Wright also called for continued consideration of liquefied natural gas export applications to countries without U.S. free-trade agreements. Other directives included reviewing appliance efficiency standards, refilling the Strategic Petroleum Reserve, modernizing nuclear weapons systems, accelerating commercial nuclear development and strengthening the electric grid. The order instructed officials to use legal authorities to streamline permitting and support energy infrastructure. These measures established the department's priorities and requested reviews; they were distinct from specific grant cancellations or completed changes to individual projects. Wright presented expanded energy supply, affordability and reliability as the administration's guiding objectives for the department.
